what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: Three hours, 8 commits, four substantive, and the shape of the project changed underneath the previous direction rather than following it. First, correct the brief: it reports that NONE of the previous focus was drawn. That is false, and the reason it is false is already written down -- `docs/staging/WORKER_FINDING_THE_STEER_EFFECTIVENESS_CONTROL_CANNOT_SEE_LANE_ZERO_AT_ALL_2026-08-27.md`. Three of four items were worked and landed: S1 landed at `bca9bb3af` and its weights were re-derived from published evidence at `898d78239` (Ofgem/BMG 2024, n=3,235, savings-importance 41% overall and 35-44% across every reported subgroup); the A/B document's 2019 forward pointer landed at `bafa625d1` along with `--level-arm` as a committed mode with 9 mutation-proven tests, which turned the level-vs-selection split from an ad-hoc invocation into something a commit can reproduce; and `CAN_THE_COMPANY_LEARN_PRICE_SENSITIVITY.md` landed at `88f5dcc61` with the predicted answer -- the declared channel bands `get_churn_estimate`, which is the company's own belief and not an observation of behaviour, so it carries none of S1's signal. Only EP1 went unworked, for the seventh time, and I now think the reason is mine and not the lever's: it was ranked last every time, and Lane 0 items are worked in my order until the tick runs out. Second, and this is the real event of the stretch: the director spoke twice at 16:03Z and 16:36Z and moved the work himself. He ruled that the marginals come from published evidence and are to be cited; that the Ofgem subgroup range is a BETWEEN-group statistic and elasticity is close to orthogonal to observables, so genuine within-segment variance must be drawn; that whether switching keys on pounds saved or percent saved must be ESTABLISHED and the world fixed if it differs; and that a trait claiming discoverability with no observable must either be given a channel or marked hidden, without waiting for him. All four are being answered right now -- 188 uncommitted lines across the three simulation files turn `price_sensitivity_for_customer` into a continuous `price_elasticity_for_customer` (`PRICE_ELASTICITY_SEGMENT_R2 = 0.02`, chosen deliberately against our own thesis) and re-scale the price response to the household's own billed pounds rather than one market-average bill; `channel_pref` is flipped to hidden with the reason written; and a new untracked control, `tests/simulation/test_discoverability_claims_are_enforced.py`, makes the curriculum's own discoverability claim falsifiable. That is the best world-side work this project has done and it is a genuine raise of the ceiling the director named. **And none of it has been scored, because both instruments that would score it are broken right now.** The three-arm A/B on the S1 world was launched correctly at 15:08:25Z under `setsid` with a START/END wrapper, and it was killed without a traceback at 15:12:53Z, 4m28s in, still inside the first arm; there is no `END rc=` line and no artefact, and **2h12m passed before this orientation noticed**, with the Lane 0 file still parked in `in_progress/` saying the run is in flight. The alarm about it fired and is sitting untracked in the staging root, drawn by nobody. Meanwhile the noise-floor measurement that would tell us whether the -£1,388.80 selection figure is signal at all is running two seeds as I write, and it patches `pdraw.price_sensitivity_for_customer` -- a symbol the churn decision stopped calling about nine minutes before those processes started. `price_elasticity_for_customer` calls `_draw_curriculum_axis` directly and never routes through the old name, so the patch reaches nothing, both seeds will return identical nets, and that identity will read as a tight instrument when it is the signature of a dead knob. This is the catalogued failure exactly: bit-for-bit reproduction across a world change is BLINDNESS, not stability. So the honest read is that nothing went backwards and the world got materially richer, but the project has started widening the world faster than it can measure the effect, and measurement debt is now the binding constraint rather than world thinness. One correction I owe against my own predecessors, including me: two directions have asserted that the CLV "cannot tell its accounts apart", citing 33 of 33 accounts recovering exactly 0.05. The ledger's own `hazard_calibration` block, which nobody read, shows seven distinct believed hazards across 401 decisions -- and in the 0.05 bucket, 263 decisions with 14 churns, the belief is nearly right (believed over realised 0.939) while the 0.08 bucket is 7.6x too pessimistic. The collapse is a property of the 33-account graded slice, which is selected on the outcome and whose excluded counterpart is 2.96x richer, not of the estimator. That was inferred and stated as observed, which is the R9 line.

focus.what: The level-vs-selection noise floor is being measured with a patch that reaches nothing, and the repair is to make it a committed mode rather than fix the scratchpad. Observed, from the code: `simulation/population_draw.py` now defines BOTH `price_sensitivity_for_customer` (line 997, at HEAD, now unused by the churn decision) and `price_elasticity_for_customer` (line 1055, working tree); `simulation/customer_events.py:313-315` imports and calls the second; and the in-flight measurement at `/tmp/claude-1000/-/16aaaff2-7e7e-417f-83d5-80457b2eaadb/scratchpad/noise_floor.py:40` reassigns `pdraw.price_sensitivity_for_customer`. `price_elasticity_for_customer` calls `_draw_curriculum_axis` directly and never routes through the old name, so the seed never reaches the decision. FIRST, cheaply: if those two PIDs are still alive, read their `SWEEP` lines when they land and check whether the two seeds returned IDENTICAL nets -- identical output across two seeds is the confirmation, and a non-identical one refutes this whole item, in which case say so and close it. THEN build the durable form: add a noise-floor mode to `tools/run_value_cycle_ab.py` that re-draws the elasticity assignment across N seeds and reports the spread in `selection_gbp` and `level_share_of_advantage`, resolving the symbol through the SAME import the decision uses so a future rename disconnects the runner loudly instead of silently. Two further defects to carry across while you are in there: the scratchpad pins the level arm at the remembered `renewal_margin_flat_level_gbp_per_mwh=44.5`, which is not the arm the committed runner runs (it reads the value arm's own realised median off the same run), so it is the noise floor of a different instrument; and the delete-the-dead-symbol question -- `price_sensitivity_for_customer` should either lose its last caller and go, or keep one and be documented as the segment-level draw, never sit there as a live-looking name nothing calls. R15 both ways: the mutation that must go red is patching the OLD name and asserting the spread stays zero.
focus.why: Every money reading this project has published in two days rests on a difference of £1,388.80 between two arms over roughly thirty renewals, and nobody has ever measured what that difference does when nothing changes but the draw. That is the number the director will be shown, and the instrument measuring its error bars is currently disconnected in a way that returns the most flattering possible answer. It goes first because it is minutes of reading plus a contained change, because the wrong reading is due to arrive within the hour, and because it makes item two's re-run worth running at all -- a second row whose error bars are unknown is a number, not evidence. Finished when a committed mode exists that a commit can reproduce, its symbol resolution cannot silently detach, a mutation on the old name reds it, and the spread across seeds is stated beside the -£1,388.80 so a reader can see whether the selection leg is distinguishable from zero. If the spread turns out to be wider than the effect, that FINISHES this item and it is the most valuable outcome available -- it means the level-vs-selection instrument cannot yet resolve what we have been asking it, and every reading built on it needs the caveat.

Two R15 traps to avoid, both catalogued in this project's own record: the check must not pass when an axis is missing, absent or malformed from the curriculum file, and it must not pass by importing the function it is meant to prove is called -- prove the wiring from the decision's side, the way the S1 test does. focus.why: A curriculum that promises a discovery channel which does not exist is the single most thesis-corrosive defect available here, because it makes the company look weak for failing at something that was impossible -- a supplier that tried to learn `channel_pref` would have been right to try and would have failed forever, and we would have read that as a poor model. The thesis says the advantage must come from INFERENCE and never ACCESS; the mirror of that is that a declared inference route must be real. The director delegated this explicitly, so it needs no further word from him, and my previous direction told a tick NOT to touch this file under R13 -- that instruction is superseded and I am recording the reversal rather than letting it sit as a live contradiction. Fourth because it is a control rather than a measurement and nothing above it waits on it. Finished when the control is committed, covers every declared axis rather than the two just fixed, is mutation-proven to fire on a fabricated channel note, and the curriculum file contains no discoverability claim that the build does not implement.
